Title: EPIC 0 — Human Gates
Summary: Clear all human-only blockers for infrastructure, API access, and data access before technical delivery proceeds.
Acceptance Criteria: All required external accounts and tokens exist and are stored securely. | The VPS and data-access prerequisites are confirmed. | Downstream infrastructure and automation work is unblocked.

Title: EPIC 1 — Codebase Audit And Re-Baseline
Summary: Re-baseline product, architecture, navigation, and planning artifacts to the new Tarteel-inspired target while preserving working foundations.
Acceptance Criteria: Asset-inventory, product, architecture, and navigation docs reflect the new target. | Existing high-value foundations are explicitly preserved. | The repo now has a canonical roadmap for the new plan.

Title: EPIC 2 — VPS Infrastructure Setup
Summary: Stand up the target runtime on the VPS with n8n, Supabase, Whisper.cpp, and Groq-backed OpenClaw.
Acceptance Criteria: Core services run on the VPS. | Health-check automation verifies the runtime regularly. | Security and network boundaries are confirmed.

Title: EPIC 3 — Data Foundation
Summary: Import Quranic text, reference audio metadata, and timestamp data into Supabase for the app and scoring workflows.
Acceptance Criteria: Supabase contains the Quranic reference schema and imported content. | Al-Fatiha data is verified end to end. | Import scripts are idempotent and reusable.

Title: EPIC 4 — Automation And Agent Stack Upgrade
Summary: Migrate and upgrade the automation layer and agent runtime for the VPS target environment.
Acceptance Criteria: VPS n8n has the required workflows. | GitHub and Plane automations are upgraded to the new runtime. | Agent runtime skills are versioned and aligned to the new roles.

Title: EPIC 5 — Core App Refactor
Summary: Refactor the app to deliver the Phase 1 Tarteel-aligned user journey end to end.
Acceptance Criteria: A signed-in user can browse, listen, record, score, and review results. | The Phase 1 user journey is runnable on device. | The preserved foundations remain intact and tests stay green.

Title: EPIC 6 — AI Core
Summary: Replace mock analysis with the real Whisper scoring pipeline while preserving confidence-aware trust rules.
Acceptance Criteria: Real audio can be scored end to end. | Confidence gating is enforced in stored and rendered results. | Validation evidence exists before stronger learner-facing claims.

Title: EPIC 7 — Phase 2 Features
Summary: Add memorization and progress features after the Phase 1 and AI core paths are validated.
Acceptance Criteria: Memorization and progress features build on the stable Phase 1 flow. | Progress data comes from real recitation sessions. | Phase 2 remains scoped after the Phase 1 launch.

Title: Purchase Hostinger KVM 4 VPS
Summary: Provision the target Hostinger VPS and confirm SSH and OpenClaw access.
Acceptance Criteria: The VPS is provisioned and reachable over SSH. | OpenClaw is visible and running. | Access details are stored securely outside the repo.

Title: Create Groq free account and store API key
Summary: Create the Groq account and secure the API key for the VPS agent runtime.
Acceptance Criteria: The account exists with a working API key. | The key is stored securely and not committed to the repo. | A test request succeeds.

Title: Generate GitHub Personal Access Token for n8n automation
Summary: Create the GitHub token needed for webhook and PR automations.
Acceptance Criteria: The token exists with the required repo scopes. | The token is stored securely. | Automation can use the token without manual re-entry.

Title: Generate Plane API key for n8n automation
Summary: Create the Plane token and capture the workspace and project identifiers.
Acceptance Criteria: The token exists and is stored securely. | Workspace slug and project ID are recorded. | Plane automation has the required credentials.

Title: Sign up at QUL and confirm Al-Husary data availability
Summary: Confirm the required QUL reference data is available for the planned scoring architecture.
Acceptance Criteria: QUL access is confirmed. | Al-Husary ayah audio and timestamps are verified or an alternative is reported. | The data-foundation plan can proceed with confidence.

Title: Confirm Tarteel API is still unavailable (final check)
Summary: Perform one final check for a public Tarteel API before the architecture proceeds without it.
Acceptance Criteria: Tarteel API status is confirmed. | If an API exists, the plan is revisited before Epic 6. | If no API exists, the current architecture assumption stands.

Title: Audit existing codebase against new Tarteel-aligned target
Summary: Classify current assets as keep, refactor, replace, or retire against the new product direction.
Acceptance Criteria: The repo has a written asset inventory. | Protected foundations are called out explicitly. | The audit is based on current code, not assumptions.

Title: Update product vision and scope docs to Tarteel-aligned target
Summary: Refresh the canonical product docs to match the new launch and Phase 2 direction.
Acceptance Criteria: Vision and MVP scope reflect the new launch target. | Tarteel alignment is documented explicitly. | User stories match the new flow.
Notes: Completed in docs/product/vision.md, docs/product/mvp-scope.md, docs/product/user-stories.md, and docs/product/tarteel-alignment.md.

Title: Update architecture docs to reflect new infrastructure
Summary: Refresh system and audio architecture docs for the VPS, Supabase, Whisper, and Groq runtime model.
Acceptance Criteria: System overview reflects the new runtime split. | Audio pipeline reflects Supabase and asynchronous scoring. | Infrastructure boundaries are documented.
Notes: Completed in docs/architecture/system-overview.md, docs/architecture/audio-pipeline.md, and docs/architecture/infrastructure.md.

Title: Produce keep/replace decision for navigation and screen structure
Summary: Define the target screen map for Phase 1 and Phase 2 and classify what exists today.
Acceptance Criteria: The new screen hierarchy is documented. | Existing screens are classified as keep-refactor, replace, or new-build. | No premature implementation is mixed into the audit.

Title: Add n8n to docker-compose.yml alongside OpenClaw
Summary: Add and boot the n8n service on the VPS next to the existing OpenClaw runtime.
Acceptance Criteria: n8n is accessible on the VPS. | An admin account is created. | The service is running under Docker.

Title: Deploy Supabase self-hosted via Docker
Summary: Deploy the self-hosted Supabase stack on the VPS and isolate it on the internal network.
Acceptance Criteria: Supabase Studio is accessible. | Anon and service-role keys are captured securely. | OpenClaw cannot reach Supabase directly.

Title: Install and test Whisper.cpp on VPS
Summary: Install Whisper.cpp in server mode and verify Arabic transcription performance on the VPS.
Acceptance Criteria: Whisper.cpp is installed and reachable over HTTP. | Arabic audio transcription succeeds. | Response time is acceptable for the planned early cohort.

Title: Configure OpenClaw to use Groq API
Summary: Configure OpenClaw to use Groq as its reasoning backend and verify workflow triggering.
Acceptance Criteria: OpenClaw uses Groq rather than local Ollama. | Reasoning and code models are configured. | OpenClaw can trigger n8n successfully.

Title: Build Workflow 0 — Health check
Summary: Create the first VPS n8n workflow to verify Supabase, Whisper, and Groq health regularly.
Acceptance Criteria: The workflow runs every five minutes. | Results are logged to agent operations storage. | Failures are captured without noisy human escalation on the first miss.

Title: Create Supabase database schema for agent operations
Summary: Create the operational tables and extensions required for agent memory and workflow logging.
Acceptance Criteria: Agent memory and logging tables exist. | pgvector is enabled for future use. | The health-check workflow can write logs successfully.

Title: Create Supabase schema for Quranic content
Summary: Create the Supabase schema for Surahs, words, reference audio, and timestamps.
Acceptance Criteria: The Quranic content tables exist with indexes. | Foreign keys are valid. | The schema supports ayah-level lookup and timing retrieval.

Title: Download QUL data assets
Summary: Download the required QUL JSON assets and upload reference audio to Supabase Storage.
Acceptance Criteria: Required JSON data exists in the repo data folder. | Audio files are uploaded to the storage bucket rather than committed to git. | The import scripts have the source assets they need.

Title: Write and run QUL import scripts
Summary: Create idempotent scripts that load Surahs, words, timestamps, and audio metadata into Supabase.
Acceptance Criteria: The import scripts are idempotent. | Core row counts are populated. | At least Al-Fatiha is fully usable for testing.

Title: Verify data integrity with test queries
Summary: Verify that imported Quranic content and reference audio metadata are correct and queryable.
Acceptance Criteria: The verification queries pass for Al-Fatiha. | Timing data is ordered and complete for the tested slice. | The imported dataset is usable for Phase 1.

Title: Migrate existing n8n workflow definitions to VPS
Summary: Import the checked-in n8n workflows into the VPS runtime and update runtime-specific credentials and URLs.
Acceptance Criteria: Checked-in workflow definitions are imported to the VPS runtime. | Runtime credentials and URLs are updated safely. | Workflows activate without import errors.

Title: Build GitHub → Plane automation workflow
Summary: Create a push-triggered workflow that summarizes branch activity and comments on or creates the corresponding Plane task.
Acceptance Criteria: Push events are received and summarized. | The correct Plane task is commented on or created. | The workflow logs its actions.

Title: Build GitHub PR → automated code review workflow
Summary: Create a PR review workflow that posts Groq review comments only when CodeRabbit has not already handled the review.
Acceptance Criteria: PR events trigger the workflow. | Duplicate bot reviews are avoided when CodeRabbit is already active. | Review actions are logged.

Title: Build Plane new task → decomposition workflow
Summary: Create a Plane-triggered decomposition workflow that expands sufficiently detailed work into child tasks.
Acceptance Criteria: Well-described tasks are decomposed into subtasks. | Vague tasks are flagged for clarification instead. | All actions are logged.

Title: Build daily standup workflow
Summary: Create a weekday standup workflow that summarizes recent commits, open tasks, and failed agent runs.
Acceptance Criteria: The workflow runs on weekday mornings Cairo time. | The summary covers completed work, in-progress work, and blockers. | The summary is posted back into the execution system.

Title: Update and version all skills.md files for new agent roles
Summary: Create the runtime skills set for orchestration, review, planning, connectors, error handling, standups, specs, and speech QA.
Acceptance Criteria: The required skills files exist. | Each skill has version and model metadata. | The agent runtime roles are aligned to the new plan.
Notes: Completed in the repo-level skills/ directory.

Title: Configure Supabase client in app
Summary: Add the Supabase client to the app without breaking the existing analysis-service abstraction.
Acceptance Criteria: The app has a typed Supabase client entrypoint. | Environment variables are documented and wired safely. | Tests and type checks remain green.

Title: Implement user authentication screens
Summary: Add sign-in and sign-up flows backed by Supabase Auth and route users into the new app flow.
Acceptance Criteria: Auth screens render and use the shared i18n pattern. | Users can sign up, sign in, and sign out. | Navigation respects auth state.

Title: Build Home / Dashboard screen
Summary: Create the authenticated landing screen with quick entry into recitation practice and recent session context.
Acceptance Criteria: The home screen renders for signed-in users. | It shows an empty state or the latest session summary. | The quick-start flow opens the Surah browser.

Title: Build Surah browser screen
Summary: Create the searchable Surah browser backed by Supabase Quran metadata.
Acceptance Criteria: All 114 Surahs are browsable. | Search works correctly. | Selecting a Surah opens the Mushaf screen.

Title: Build Mushaf reader screen with reference audio playback
Summary: Create the Mushaf view with ayah-level playback and word highlighting backed by reference timestamps.
Acceptance Criteria: Quran text displays correctly in Arabic. | Reference audio plays per ayah. | Word highlighting and ayah recording entry points work.

Title: Refactor recording screen for production audio capture
Summary: Upgrade the existing recording screen from a shell into a real ayah-context capture, playback, and submission flow.
Acceptance Criteria: The recording screen receives ayah context as route params. | Users can record, replay, and submit audio. | Submission triggers the scoring path and shows loading state.

Title: Build recitation result screen
Summary: Create the result screen with overall score, word statuses, retry, and navigation actions.
Acceptance Criteria: The result screen shows overall and word-level feedback. | Low-confidence words render as uncertain rather than wrong. | Try-again and next-ayah actions work correctly.

Title: Create Supabase schema for app user data
Summary: Create the user profile and recitation-session tables with row-level security.
Acceptance Criteria: The user and session tables exist. | RLS policies are active. | Basic insert and select behavior works for a user.

Title: Build session history screen
Summary: Move session history to Supabase-backed user data while preserving the repository abstraction pattern.
Acceptance Criteria: History loads from Supabase rather than only local storage. | Sessions are listed per user. | Past result detail can be reopened.

Title: End-to-end smoke test of Phase 1 user journey
Summary: Validate the full launch journey from auth through result and history on a real device or simulator.
Acceptance Criteria: The complete Phase 1 journey passes end to end. | Any failures are captured as follow-up tasks. | No crashes or unhandled errors appear during the flow.

Title: Build Whisper transcription service on VPS
Summary: Create the thin transcription service that exposes Whisper results to the scoring workflow.
Acceptance Criteria: The service accepts audio uploads and returns text, word timings, and confidence. | Arabic transcription works for test audio. | n8n can call the service.

Title: Build audio scoring workflow in n8n
Summary: Create the scoring workflow that turns pending sessions into scored sessions using Whisper and reference data.
Acceptance Criteria: Pending sessions trigger the workflow. | Confidence gating is enforced in stored word results. | Scored sessions are written back to Supabase with logs.

Title: Replace mock analysis service with real Supabase polling
Summary: Swap the fixture-backed analysis implementation for the real upload and polling flow while preserving the interface contract.
Acceptance Criteria: The analysis-service interface remains unchanged. | Real audio uploads and polling work. | Mock fixtures remain available for test paths.

Title: Validate scoring accuracy on Surah Al-Fatiha
Summary: Run the validation cases for correct, incorrect, silent, and fast recitation before treating real scoring as ship-ready.
Acceptance Criteria: All planned test cases are executed and documented. | If scores are weak, the ship posture is adjusted rather than overclaimed. | The validation report exists in repo docs.

Title: Build hidden verses memorization mode
Summary: Add the Phase 2 memorization mode on top of the Mushaf and scoring flow.
Acceptance Criteria: The mode can hide text. | Correct recitation reveals text progressively. | Mode state resets cleanly between sessions.

Title: Build goals and streaks system
Summary: Add Phase 2 goal and streak features on top of authenticated recitation-session data.
Acceptance Criteria: Goal and streak data is stored correctly. | The goals screen renders the current state. | Streaks update from real session activity.

Title: Build mistake history and progress screen
Summary: Add Phase 2 trend and mistake-history views using recitation-session results.
Acceptance Criteria: The screen shows per-Surah progress trends. | Frequent mistakes are derived correctly from stored results. | The visualizations work with at least one real user dataset.
